title: Session re-auth propagation, JIT group sync, and admin-driven revocation for SAML
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Background: Production customers are asking for tighter session controls when using SAML SSO: ability to require re-auth (step-up) for high-privilege console routes, immediate session revocation via admin controls, consistent propagation of logout across devices, and reliable JIT provisioning that maps IdP groups to RBAC v2 roles. Current behaviors are inconsistent across IdPs and we lack structured audit events for session lifecycle (create/extend/reauth/invalidate).

Goals:
- Define and implement a consistent session model for SAML that includes IdP session binding (idp_session_index + nameID), device binding, MFA level, and assertion metadata.
- Implement re-auth (step-up) enforcement for configured routes using SAML ACR values or forced SP-initiated reauth when IdP returned AC R is insufficient.
- Ensure JIT provisioning performs deterministic group->role mapping for RBAC v2 and emits audit events for every mapping change.
- Provide admin APIs/UI to locally invalidate all sessions for a user, per-device logout, and force a re-auth requirement for next access.
- Propagate IdP-initiated and SP-initiated logout properly across all active sessions/devices and record audit events for each affected session.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) New session data model persists: session_id, user_id, idp, idp_session_index, saml_nameid, assertion_id, authn_instant, device_id (optional), mfa_level, acr, created_at, expires_at, last_activity. Stored values must be emit-able in audit logs (no PII beyond nameID hash).
2) Route-level policy config (console.route: ["billing","admin/settings"]) can be marked requiring_stepup:true. When user session lacks required mfa_level or acr, system triggers SP-initiated SAML AuthnRequest with requested_authn_context set to configured ACR URI.
3) Admin Revocation API: POST /admin/users/{id}/sessions/invalidate supports: all_devices | device:{id} | except_device:{id}. Calling this invalidates sessions immediately; response includes list of invalidated session_ids and audit event ids.
4) JIT provisioning: when a new SAML assertion contains group attributes, we map groups -> RBAC v2 roles deterministically using ordering precedence table. Role deltas (created/removed) are logged as JIT_ROLE_ASSIGNMENT events.
5) Logout propagation: IdP-initiated logout with SessionIndex must find and invalidate all sessions tied to that idp_session_index; if IdP does not provide SessionIndex we fall back to matching nameID + last_authn_instant window.
6) Audit logging: emit structured audit events (SAML_ASSERTION_VERIFIED, SESSION_CREATED, SESSION_EXTENDED, MFA_STEPUP_REQUIRED, MFA_STEPUP_COMPLETED, SESSION_INVALIDATED, LOGOUT_INITIATED, LOGOUT_COMPLETED, JIT_ROLE_ASSIGNMENT). Event payloads must include: timestamp, actor_user_id, actor_type (user|admin|system), session_id, idp, assertion_id, ip, user_agent, route (if applicable), outcome, correlation_id.
7) Backwards compatibility: existing hosted customers see no visible break during rollout; fallback to prior behavior if assertion fails or IdP unresponsive.

Proposed design notes: 
- Session model: add fields to sessions table and caching layer (Redis) with TTL aligned to assertion expiration but with local renewal policy for long-running console sessions. Store only hashed nameIDs in logs.
- Re-auth flow: for SP-initiated step-up we will generate an AuthnRequest with RequestedAuthnContext including the required ACRs. If IdP returns a lower ACR, present UI and block sensitive route until successful re-auth. Document UX with Design.
- JIT group sync: expand JIT handler to accept groups attribute (multi-valued). Apply mapping table ordered by specificity (explicit group->role rules, wildcard rules, default role). Emit JIT_ROLE_ASSIGNMENT events; record the mapping version used for auditability.
- Logout handling: implement a two-pass invalidation on IdP-initiated logout: 1) match by SessionIndex (preferred), 2) fallback to nameID + authn_instant < 5m window. For SP-initiated logout, attempt IdP SingleLogout via front-channel and back-channel where supported; always mark local sessions invalidated regardless of IdP response to avoid hung sessions.
- Admin controls: expose APIs and Console actions: "Force logout (all devices)", "Invalidate device", "Require immediate re-auth". These must be gated by new admin permission scope (rbac:admin.sessions.invalidate).

Implementation plan (milestones):
- M1 (design & spec) 2w: detailed design doc, API spec, logging schema, UX mockups.
- M2 (core infra) 3w: extend session schema, add Redis cache fields, implement admin invalidation APIs, unit tests.
- M3 (SAML flows) 3w: implement step-up AuthnRequest, IdP logout handling, JIT group mapping logic, integration tests with Okta and Azure AD.
- M4 (audit & observability) 2w: structured event emission, dashboards for session counts/invalidations/reauth rate, alerting for unusual mass invalidations.
- M5 (canary rollout) 2w: opt-in orgs -> staged rollout across regions, monitor metrics and customer support tickets.

Monitoring & SLOs:
- Metric: sessions.invalidated_per_minute (alert if > 10x baseline for a given org).
- Metric: stepup_success_rate per route (>95%).
- Metric: JIT_role_assignment_errors (<0.5%).
- Audit retention: session lifecycle events retained for 365 days for enterprise customers; 30 days for free tier.

Testing plan:
- Automated e2e tests against mock IdP supporting ACR negotiation, session index, and group attributes.
- Integration tests with Okta and Azure AD tenant test accounts.
- Chaos tests: simulate clock skew, assertion replay, and IdP downtime to validate fallback paths.
- Penetration test for session fixation and replay.

Rollout & migration notes:
- Add feature flag auth.saml.session_v2_enabled per org. Default off. Gradually enable for pilot customers.
- Migrate sessions lazily: if an old session is used, enrich it with new fields on access; do not force re-login during migration unless security policy requires.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should we accept lower ACR and do local 2FA if IdP lacks MFA? (security vs UX). Recommendation: prefer IdP-provided MFA for enterprise compliance, but provide fallback step-up via Redwood-hosted MFA only after security review.
- How to handle SLO for IdP-initiated logout when IdP sends malformed SessionIndex? We use nameID fallback and emit a diagnostic_audit event.

Related docs/links: Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Security/pages/SAML+Session+V2 (placeholder), GH PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pulls, Okta test tenant guide (internal drive link).
